target_customer: B2B SaaS sales and presales teams that show product demos to prospects
problem: Sales teams struggle to give prospects hands-on demos without engineering effort, and cannot see how prospects engage with a demo afterwards.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for interactive demo creation and engagement analytics
product_category: interactive product demo and sales enablement software

founders.name: Bryan Houlton
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder with a link to orinlabs.org; Navattic's June 2023 post calls him CEO of Manatee. No education or employers found in opened sources.

founders.name: Ryan Downing
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder with the title Engineer at Navattic (the acquirer-partner, so likely current at the time the page was updated). The launch post calls Ryan the co-founder.

exit.reason: Navattic announced that Manatee was joining forces with it; terms and structure not disclosed.

competitors.name: Walnut
competitors.what: No-code personalized product demo and analytics platform for sales teams
competitors.traction_then: Reported growth of 700% in four months by January 2022
competitors.funding_then: $35M Series B in January 2022, about $56M total per press

competitors.name: Reprise
competitors.what: No-code product demo platform for sales and marketing teams
competitors.funding_then: $62M Series B in November 2021 led by ICONIQ Growth

technical_complexity.rationale: Capturing a live product front end, anonymizing data and keeping demos in sync with frontend changes, plus engagement tracking, is standard engineering with some hard parts for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Well funded rivals Walnut and Reprise already sold demo software and a sandbox approach could be copied; no data or network effect moat is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rather than being copied, the team joined Navattic in June 2023, a direct competitor in interactive demos.

market_need_then: The YC launch post says teams relied on engineering built demo deployments or edited screenshots in Photoshop or Figma, and that Walnut and Reprise had limited use cases without a sandbox. Venture rounds into Walnut and Reprise in late 2021 and early 2022 show demand for demo software.

branding.domain_note: Used trymanatee.com rather than manatee.com (YC page lists trymanatee.com).

identity.logo: A manatee logo shown on the YC page; no further description found
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and direct in the launch post, framed as DocSend for demos

brand_strength.rationale: No press, merch or community found about the brand itself; several unrelated companies share the name Manatee, which makes search results confusable.

outcome_analysis: Manatee launched an interactive demo tool in YC Summer 2022 against Walnut and Reprise, which had raised large rounds months earlier. With a two person team and a reported 500 thousand dollar pre-seed, it joined its competitor Navattic in June 2023, about a year after the batch. Terms and the reason were not disclosed, so this reads as a soft landing into a better funded rival rather than a confirmed shutdown for lack of traction.
notes: Company site trymanatee.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch (likely dead). Pre-seed of 500K in 2022-08 rests on a single database (VCBacked, also Extruct); no second outlet. CB Insights shows 11.59M over 6 rounds for a Manatee but that is likely a different company (a children's mental health startup also named Manatee), so it is excluded. The Navattic deal was described only as joining forces; acquisition terms unknown. Navattic is not listed as a 2022 competitor because no source dated near the batch was found; it is recorded as the later partner in exit. The YC launch post is undated in the fetch, estimated near the batch.
